title: de.hubtask.work.recurrence.occurrence_created.v1
description: A series produced an entry: the occurrence a recurrence rule owed for a moment on its grid (D-05). It is published beside the entry's own item.created rather than instead of it - what happened to the world is that an entry came into being - and what it adds is the connection between the series, the template it was copied from and the entry that came out. Single-value enums stand in for `const`, and the bounds of a value are stated in its description rather than as keywords: the contract test validates against this file with the subset of JSON Schema the project implements, and a keyword it silently ignored would be a promise nobody checks. The wire format is a CloudEvent 1.0 in structured JSON (ADR-0007); the tenant, the actor and the causal chain travel as CloudEvents extension attributes, whose names are lower case without separators as the specification requires. Fields may be added; removing or reinterpreting one requires a .v2 delivered alongside .v1 for at least two minor releases (domain-model.md §4).

id.description: UUIDv7. Stable across delivery attempts, so a consumer deduplicates on it (at-least-once delivery).

source.description: The installation and the bounded context that produced the event.

subject.description: What the event is about, so that a consumer can filter without parsing the payload.

actorid.description: Absent when the system itself acts. No label: an event leaves the installation, and a name is personal data a subscriber does not need in order to react (ADR-0018).

onbehalfof.description: The principal an automation rule or an agent runs as.

correlationid.description: Everything that came out of one original action carries the same value. A root event is its own correlation.

causationid.description: The event that caused this one. Absent for an action a person took.

causationdepth.description: Distance from the original action. The rule engine stops at 5 and marks the run ABORTED_LOOP (automation.md §2).

data.description: Which series, which template, which entry, and which moment of the rule's grid it is. The moment is the rule's computed time rather than the clock's: an occurrence materialised late is still that morning's occurrence, and a consumer reconstructing the series needs the grid rather than the bookkeeping.

source_item_id.description: The entry the series sits on - the template the occurrence was copied from.

collection_id.description: The collection the occurrence belongs to, and the one an actor's permission to see it is judged against.

occurrence_at.description: The moment of the rule's grid this entry is, RFC 3339 in UTC (i18n-l10n.md §7).
